question: What is the primary function of surgical swabs in the operating theatre?
explanation: Surgical swabs are primarily used to soak up fluids and maintain a clear view of the operating site. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why do standard surgical swabs contain a radiopaque marker?

options.A: To make them visible under X-ray imaging
options.B: To increase their fluid absorption capacity
options.C: To prevent them from sticking to raw tissues
options.D: To change color when exposed to blood

explanation: The radiopaque strip allows healthcare teams to locate a lost swab inside a patient using an X-ray machine. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which surgical sponge is the largest and used for packing off bowels during abdominal procedures?
explanation: Laparotomy sponges are large pads designed to handle major fluid volumes and hold back large organs. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h2)

question: What type of swab is tiny, rolled, and held on forceps during throat surgeries?
explanation: Tonsil sponges are specifically sized for small cavities like the throat and are handled strictly with forceps. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h2)

question: Who is primarily responsible for recording the counts on the whiteboard in the theatre?
explanation: The circulating nurse stays unsterile to document and maintain the running tally of all counts. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h3)

question: Why must the scrub nurse and circulating nurse count swabs out loud together?

options.A: To fulfill a hospital routine without much attention
options.B: To ensure both parties hear and agree on the exact tally
options.C: To help the surgeon concentrate on the incision
options.D: To entertain the rest of the surgical team

explanation: Verbalizing numbers simultaneously prevents individual miscalculation and guarantees accountability. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h3)

question: When must the very first baseline swab count be performed?
explanation: An initial count establishes the baseline quantity before any item enters the patient's body. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h4)

question: A nurse performs the final swab count at which specific surgical milestone?
explanation: The final count happens during skin closure to ensure nothing was left behind before the wound is completely sealed. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the immediate action when a swab count is reported as incorrect?

options.A: Ignore the discrepancy if it is only one swab
options.B: Wait until the patient wakes up to ask
options.C: Inform the surgeon and halt wound closure

explanation: Closing the wound with a missing item worsens the medical and legal consequences, so the surgeon must stop immediately. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h5)

question: What diagnostic tool is used inside the theatre when a swab cannot be found?
explanation: Radiopaque threads in swabs make them visible under X-ray, helping locate the missing item inside the body. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why should surgical sponges NEVER be used for post-operative wound dressings?

options.A: They are too expensive for dressings
options.C: They dissolve too quickly in air
options.D: It confuses the official count records

explanation: Using countable items as dressings creates confusion about whether an item is inside the patient or on top of the skin. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)

question: The main goal of implementing strict swab counting protocols in Nigerian hospitals is to achieve what outcome?

options.B: Minimizing the need for scrub nurses
options.D: Reducing the cost of hospital linen

explanation: All counting procedures are primarily designed to ensure zero items are left inside patients. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)
